correctness.rationale: The frozen proof's distinct-side zero-set classification (RESULT.md line 37) is false and leaves out configurations needed for its compactness argument. For example, in the triangle with vertices (0,0),(1,0),(0,1), select (1/2,0) on the bottom edge and select (0,0),(1,0) on its two neighboring edges. This is a zero-area triple on three selected sides with no coincidence. Zero endpoint probability does not justify ignoring its neighborhoods in a sublevel-volume bound. The theorem itself is not contradicted. The atom follows from collinearity on a common supporting face, not from coincidences. The incident repeated-edge integral is exactly 2x log(1/x)+x^2 for x=2t/(ab sin theta) in (0,1); the assignment weight 3a^2b/L^3 gives the stated constant. Nonincident pairs have altitude bounded below. A valid repair of the distinct-side estimate would include both coincidence lines and the lines with the middle point on the supporting side and its endpoints occupied from the neighboring sides. On a coincidence line at V, the two incident-direction derivatives cannot both vanish since the third point is not V. On the omitted line, writing the middle point as (aw,0) on a side of length a, the inward arclength derivatives of signed doubled area at the other two points are a(1-w)E_y and aw F_y, with both inward heights E_y,F_y positive. Thus at least one derivative is nonzero everywhere on the compact zero set. A finite local cover and one-coordinate sublevel integration then give the O_K(t) needed by the theorem. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed; it only checks finite coefficient/atom normalization and cannot establish this bound. No corrected finding is submitted because the unchanged claim is covered in full.
